holidays.name: Pluto Demoted Day
holidays.description: A day for the solar system's most famous underdog. Pluto went from beloved ninth planet to "dwarf planet" in a single vote. Fans mark the day with Pluto-themed snacks, sympathetic memes, and loud arguments that it should still be a planet.
holidays.origin: On August 24, 2006, the International Astronomical Union voted at its General Assembly in Prague to adopt a formal definition of "planet." Pluto didn't meet the criterion of clearing its orbital neighborhood, so it was reclassified as a dwarf planet.
holidays.funFact: Clyde Tombaugh discovered Pluto in 1930. An 11-year-old English girl, Venetia Burney, suggested the name, and it was a hit with astronomers.

holidays.name: National Waffle Day
holidays.description: A day for waffles with butter, syrup, fruit, whipped cream, or even fried chicken. Breakfast gets a grid-patterned excuse to be dessert.
holidays.origin: The day commemorates August 24, 1869. On that date Cornelius Swarthout of Troy, New York, patented the first waffle iron, which was a stovetop model.
holidays.funFact: Swarthout's waffle iron had a hinged design that could be flipped over the fire. That design is the ancestor of the waffle makers we use today.

holidays.name: National Peach Pie Day
holidays.description: A salute to the juicy, golden, buttery-crusted summer classic. It falls at the height of peach season, so there's plenty of ripe fruit around. Bakers are encouraged to make a pie from scratch and to eat it while it's still warm, ideally with a scoop of vanilla ice cream.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It was created to celebrate peaches at their seasonal peak in late summer.
holidays.funFact: Georgia is nicknamed the Peach State, but California grows far more peaches than any other U.S. state.
